objectives.text: Keep Atlantic LNG running on gas from Venezuela. The Dragon field is the route: Atlantic LNG produces below nameplate capacity for want of gas, and the energy minister puts the first Dragon deliveries at Q3 2027. Caracas froze the gas arrangements in October 2025, so the goal depends on Venezuela's consent.

means.text: Access to Washington. The US Treasury licence (OFAC) for the Dragon project, which the attorney general announced in October 2025, and the US warship visit of the same month are the two levers. Nation News later reports the licence revoked in April 2026, while the Trinidad Express account describes it as ongoing: the sources conflict and both are kept.

The Trinidad economy is mainly industrial and built on oil and gas reserves (Wikipedia, tier 4: a pointer, not a source of record). The gas-shortage constraint is the same fact seen from the plant: the LNG train runs below capacity.

paradoxes.text: The moves that bought US backing for the Dragon licence, the support for the boat strikes and the warship visit, are the moves Caracas used to freeze the gas accord. The alignment that unlocks Washington's permission is the one that closes the Venezuelan molecules Trinidad needs.

grand_strategy.reading: Trinidad and Tobago plays for gas. Its LNG plant runs below capacity, and the field it needs, Dragon, is shared with Venezuela, so the strategy is to buy Venezuelan molecules with a visible loyalty to Washington. That loyalty brought a US licence and a warship visit, and Caracas answered in the same month by freezing the accord; the first deliveries, due in 2027, depend on a neighbour Port of Spain has angered and a patron it has courted.

stances.note: Partner, no treaty found. Persad-Bissessar backed the US boat strikes of 2025, a US warship docked in October 2025, and the US Treasury licence for the Dragon project was announced in the same month. The grade is our reading: no source calls the relation an alliance or a partnership in those words, and the press accounts conflict on whether the licence was revoked in April 2026. Trend stable because the licence status is unsettled. Bond none: pure interest, no kinship or grievance in the sources read. Confidence C: tier 3 press only, search snippets and titles, article bodies not read.

stances.note: Rival over gas, not adversary. Caracas suspended the gas accord over the US warship visit, accused Port of Spain of a false-flag operation, and declared Persad-Bissessar persona non grata; the same month Trinidad was welcoming US forces in the Caribbean. Trend stable: the record runs from the October 2025 freeze to a 2026 move back toward talks, and a Caracas delegation was only planned. Bond none: the dispute is about molecules and the Dragon field, with no kinship or open grievance in the sources. Confidence C: our reading of the grade, tier 3 press, no source calls the relation 'rival'.

stances.note: Kin through the diaspora, not through the state. Trinidad's prime minister is of Indian origin, the first woman of Indian origin to lead a country outside India and the wider subcontinent, per Wikipedia (tier 4, a pointer only). The grade partner and the kin bond are our reading: no India-Trinidad source was read, no bilateral agreement or visit checked, and the 'since' year is independence, not a diplomatic date. This is a gap, to be filled from the two foreign ministries. Confidence C.
